Thanks again for taking the time today, Joe — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from the call: 

- Goal: Reduce inference cost and latency for Acme's customer chat assistant; target 30% lower per-token cost without impacting 95th percentile latency SLOs.
- Primary success criteria: end-to-end response time < 400ms for web traffic and total monthly inference cost below $X (TBD).
- Key stakeholders we identified on the call: you (product owner), Samir (security/infra), Procurement (contracts team), and an economic buyer (we discussed the Head of Platform).

Attached is a mutual action plan (MAP) with proposed milestones — discovery POC, security review, procurement, and pilot rollout. Can you confirm the economic buyer and who on your side handles security questionnaires? Also, what procurement timelines should we expect (e.g., standard 30/45/60 day review)?

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the name/email of the economic buyer and procurement contact.
2) Samir (or security) to confirm whether our standard security packet + SOC2 report is enough or if you need further artifacts.
3) We schedule a technical kickoff/POC scoping session next week (30–45 min).

Files attached: 2026-07-15-Acme-MAP.xlsx, Redwood-Security-Overview-v2.pdf

If it helps, we can prepare a procurement exception request (discount/SLA) to speed approvals — let me know if that would be useful.

Thanks,
Marissa

Aditya / Lauren — forwarding the thread with Acme. They asked for a procurement exception template and indicated that discount/SLA exceptions will materially speed up procurement (standard review ~45 days, exceptions may add approvals).

Key ask from Acme: procurement would like a written exception request capturing proposed discount and SLA modifications and rationale. They hinted that finance will need the cost delta and legal will need a short risks/mitigations note.

Suggested exception request we can propose: 20% first-year discount on committed Dedicated capacity + custom SLA (99.9% uptime with a 10% service credit cap) instead of our standard 99.95% & 25% cap. They want a faster start so pricing has to be competitive.

Attachments: Acme-Procurement-Request-20260721.pdf (procurement's intake form they sent).

Can you advise: 1) is 20% first-year discount approvable under current quota? 2) legal — ok to reduce our SLA cap to 10% for this deal (risks we should note)?

Thanks —
Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap + next steps (procurement & stakeholders) -- procurement exception request

Marissa — thanks for the context and the proposed terms. Quick assessment: 

- Pricing: 20% first-year discount is within the standard discount band for Strategic POCs / early-stage enterprise pilots, provided we secure a minimum 12-month committed volume. Please document committed MRR and expected token volumes in the MAP before final approval.
- SLA: reducing the service credit cap from 25% to 10% increases financial risk. Legal (Lauren) — any objections? If legal signs off, we should add a short mitigation: accelerated incident response and a 3-month SLA review clause tied to observed uptime.
- Security/Compliance: make sure Samir signs off on the SSO/KMS and data retention notes — we're not granting broad data residency exceptions.

Marissa — please prepare a short procurement exception memo (1 page) that includes: proposed discount, SLA change, committed volume, business justification, mitigation steps, and required approvals. I can pre-approve on pricing contingent on the MRR numbers; Lauren will handle legal wording.

Aditya
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap + next steps (procurement & stakeholders) -- procurement exception request

Thanks — quick legal take: 

- SLA cap: legal is generally cautious about lowering the monetary cap on credits because it limits customer remedies; however, for strategic pilots where the commercial upsides are clear, we can accept a 10% cap for the first year if the contract includes: (a) explicit scope limits, (b) incident response and escalation paths, and (c) a mandatory SLA review after 3 months.
- Contract wording: I'll prepare a short addendum that documents the exception and sets the review cadence. We should avoid language that broadens liability elsewhere.

One ask: include a short sentence in the exception memo noting that security artifacts (SOC2, network diagram, data flow) were provided and Samir has confirmed there's no data residency exception requested. That will help procurement move faster.

Lauren
